goal: Get an application for a public service approved
targetState: The applicant has received approval and can access the service.

items.label: The applicant meets the service's eligibility conditions.
items.basis: Approval cannot validly be granted if the applicant does not satisfy the substantive eligibility conditions.
items.notes: This is a substantive condition, not a prescribed administrative step.

items.label: An authorised decision-maker can grant the service.
items.basis: The approval must be made by an authority with the legal power to grant it.
items.notes: The identity of the decision-maker may vary; the existence of valid authority is the required state.

items.label: The decision-maker has enough reliable information to establish eligibility.
items.basis: The authority needs a sufficient basis to determine whether the eligibility conditions are met.
items.notes: The information requirement may be satisfied through different evidence sources.

items.label: The applicant submits the prescribed online form.
items.basis: An online form is one way to communicate the information needed for assessment.
items.notes: Alternative channels may include assisted lodgement, paper forms or an authorised representative.

items.label: The authority retrieves relevant information from an existing verified record.
items.basis: Existing records may provide some or all of the evidence needed to establish eligibility.
items.notes: This is a possible evidence pathway, subject to lawful access, accuracy and consent requirements.

items.label: The applicant attends an in-person appointment.
items.basis: An appointment may be used to verify identity or collect information, but it is not necessarily the only way to do so.
items.notes: Test whether the appointment is genuinely necessary for this applicant and service.

items.label: The applicant must use the standard online portal because that is the normal process.
items.basis: The portal may be the default route without being a necessary condition for approval.
items.notes: A standard channel should not be mistaken for a necessary state if equivalent channels can satisfy the evidence requirement.
